title: 暗号を解いた男 ― アラン・チューリング
style: 画風01・光彩のある劇場アニメ背景を基調にした写実的な科学史ドキュメンタリー
research_basis: GCHQ: Alan Turing and Bletchley Park history
Oxford Academic: Turing, Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
UK Ministry of Justice: 2013 royal pardon
timeline: 1939-1945: Turing and colleagues worked at Bletchley Park on German Enigma systems
1940 onward: the British Bombe built on crucial Polish foundations and was improved through team work
postwar: Turing worked on stored-program computing at NPL and Manchester
1950: Computing Machinery and Intelligence published in Mind
1952: prosecuted and convicted for homosexual activity then criminalized
24 December 2013: received a posthumous royal pardon

alan_turing.identity: broad oval face, strong dark eyebrows, short dark hair with a precise left side part, close-cut sides, direct deep-set eyes, broad jaw and slightly prominent ears; based on the official GCHQ portrait
alan_turing.wardrobe_wartime: rumpled brown or charcoal tweed jacket, pale striped shirt, narrow dark tie, dark trousers; practical rather than glamorous
alan_turing.wardrobe_postwar: mid-grey tweed suit and striped shirt, slightly older face
alan_turing.manner: intensely focused, quick-moving, collaborative but independent; never a lone superhero or a modern hacker

gordon_welchman.identity: slim British mathematician, high forehead, neatly combed brown hair, round spectacles
gordon_welchman.wardrobe: dark three-piece suit or tweed jacket

bombe_operators.identity: young Women's Royal Naval Service operators and mixed civilian cryptanalytic staff
bombe_operators.wardrobe: period-correct navy Wren uniform or restrained 1940s civilian clothing

technology_accuracy: Enigma is a portable electro-mechanical cipher machine with keyboard, lampboard, plugboard and rotors; no glowing digital display
the Bombe is a large wall-like electro-mechanical machine with repeated banks of rotating drums; it is not a general-purpose computer
the Bombe helps eliminate impossible rotor settings and does not automatically print fully translated messages
show human crib selection, menus, checking, Typex-like follow-up and naval intelligence interpretation as a team process
the British Bombe built on crucial Polish cryptanalytic foundations and was designed and improved by Turing, Gordon Welchman and others
postwar machine-intelligence scenes use teleprinters, paper tape and early stored-program computers, not humanoid robots or modern chat interfaces
history_accuracy: do not depict Turing as single-handedly breaking every Enigma message
do not collapse Bombe engineering, operation and intelligence analysis into one instant
do not show decoded messages exposing readable military secrets
depict 1952 prosecution through courthouse and official procedure without a sensational trial scene
do not show an apple, cyanide, suicide method, hospital death or definitive cause-of-death claim
the 2013 pardon is posthumous and must not be shown as a ceremony attended by Turing
the pardon is presented as recognition that came far too late, not as erasing the harm or conviction from history

composition.subtitle_safe_area: keep important faces, hands, machines and documents above the lower 45 percent
composition.camera: one stable push, pull or hold per shot
composition.text: no readable generated labels, secret messages, equations, newspaper headlines or signatures

avoid: The Imitation Game movie actor likenesses or copying movie compositions
modern keyboards, flat screens, LEDs, server rooms or holographic code in historical scenes
Turing working completely alone while colleagues stand idle
Bombe as a humanoid AI or an automatic plaintext printer
villainous courtroom caricatures, prison bars, conversion-therapy spectacle or graphic medical imagery
apple symbolism, cyanide imagery, ghosts, halos, fantasy electricity, readable text, logos or watermarks
